newsitem.title: ITALY: Greece willing to join Albania force - minister.
newsitem.headline: Greece willing to join Albania force - minister.

text.p: Greece is willing to contribute police or troops to a multinational security force being assembled to go to Albania with a European relief mission, deputy foreign minister George Papandreou said on Tuesday.
Papandreou said technical details of the force, which would provide protection for a European Union humanitarian mission, were still being worked out.
"We would be willing to offer either police or troops," Papandreou told Reuters after he met Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino in Rome.
"We'd be under the command of the multinational force...so they would have the say as to where we would go," he said.
Southern Albania, where armed rebels and lawless mafias have taken control of several towns, has a sizeable ethnic Greek minority.

Papandreou said Athens supported Fino's new national unity government, formed this month in response to the unrest, and had been careful not to allow the ethnic minority issue to become linked to the Balkan state's crisis.

"It has nothing to do with the Greek minority population in southern Albania," he said, adding that Greece was nonetheless concerned that attempts might be made by fringe groups to make them a scapegoat for Albania's turmoil.
Papandreou was in Rome for a meeting of EU foreign ministers on the 40th anniversary of the Treaty of Rome which founded the original European Economic Community (EEC).
Fino met the ministers and also held separate talks with Greece and Italy, the two countries which have been at the forefront of diplomatic efforts to help resolve Albania's crisis.
Fino made no comment on his discussions but told German SAT1 television on his arrival that Albania, Europe's poorest country, was in dire need of outside help.
"We are very sad that today, when we are celebrating 40 years of peace in Europe, Albania lives through these tragic times," he said.
